posts.text: Nvidia’s $235 Billion Buyback, SpaceX Milestone and Meta’s AI Push. Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Nvidia's decision to boost the size of its share buyback plan by a record $150 billion, taking the total amount to $235 billion. Plus, SpaceX's Starship rocket reaches orbit for the first time, marking a major milestone after an engine failed during ascent and briefly put the mission at risk. And, Meta taps MongoDB's president and CEO to lead a new AI platform for enterprise customers that Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg called “the next major pillar of our business.” (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: Trump, Anthropic CEO Take AI Safety Debate to Dinner. President Donald Trump and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei met for dinner as their opposing views on AI safety increasingly shape the debate over how quickly the technology should advance. Amodei has called for “pacing” development of the most advanced models and stronger guardrails, while President Trump has pushed back against slowing AI development as the US races to stay ahead of China. Bloomberg’s Mike Shepard discusses what’s known about the meeting with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: Gecko CEO: Physical AI Needs Humans in Control. Gecko Robotics CEO Jake Loosararian says the next phase of AI safety is about keeping humans in control as autonomous systems move into the physical world. He discusses Gecko’s work with Nvidia on an open agent safety platform designed to set boundaries around AI agents operating robots, including in military and industrial settings. Loosararian argues that safety and rapid deployment don’t have to be at odds. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: kimmonismus
posts.text:
Jev just made a big move on the frontier models.

The viral tiny decision model is now being used to decide which frontier model answers your prompt.

The way it does it is what's interesting. It's not a single pass like most routers.

Instead, swarms of hundreds of Jevs scan the entire conversation, score every part of it against benchmark results for Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Fable, Kimi, DeepSeek and more, then vote on who takes each step.

The reported result: 99% of Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra's performance on DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench 4.0 and SWE-Atlas. For 40% less.

That's a real problem for the labs. Their pricing depends on you running their most expensive model on everything. If a router can get you almost the same results while only calling Opus when it's actually needed, the premium tier starts to look optional.
